newsitem.title: UK: Monthly Review - Gulf and Mideast peace in danger.
newsitem.headline: Monthly Review - Gulf and Mideast peace in danger.

text.p: The U.S. rocketed southern Iraq in early September in retaliation for Baghdad's incursion into the Kurdish north while late in the month 69 people died in Israeli- Palestinian clashes which left the Middle East peace in tatters.
Islamic Taleban rebels seized the Afghan capital Kabul, sending President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government fleeing into the mountains and imposing its own strict brand of Islam.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month.
Sept 1 - The U.N. announces it is delaying implementation of the oil-for-food deal with Baghdad following Iraq's incursion into the Kurdish exclusion zone.
Sept 2 - Moslem rebels and the Philippines government sign a peace pact ending 24 years of war that killed 125,000 people.

Sept 3 - United States pounds Iraq with 27 cruise missiles at dawn, and a further 17 in the early hours of Sept 4. An extended no-fly zone reaching to the 33rd parallel comes into effect at 0800 GMT on the same day.
Sept 3 - Belgian police say they have found the bodies of two teenagers who were the subject of a Europe-wide alarm over paedophile abductors.
Sept 4 - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meets Palestinian President Yasser Arafat for their first summit.
Sept 5 - Three radical Moslems are convicted in New York of planning to bomb 12 U.S. planes to punish the United States for supporting Israel.
Sept 8 - A Turkish-Cypriot soldier is shot dead near the U.N. buffer zone separating Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
Sept 9 - Sudan and Uganda agree to resume diplomatic relations, broken in April 1995.
Sept 9 - Croatia and Yugoslavia establish full diplomatic relations, formalising an agreement made on August 23.
Sept 9 - The Iraqi-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) captures the main stronghold of Sulaimaniya from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
Sept 9 - Hutu rebels murder the Roman Catholic archbishop of Burundi, Joachim Ruhuna, and three other people in an ambush.
Sept 10 - Britain says Switzerland turned over to Allied powers only a small part of the gold it acknowledged buying in World War Two.
Sept 10 - Investigators probing Belgium's child abuse scandal question several policemen after raids.
Sept 11 - Rebel Taleban militia capture the Afghan town of Jalalabad and on Sept 13 the government confirm they have control of the eastern province of Laghman as well.

Sept 11 - Iraqi forces fire a missile at U.S. fighter planes over northern Iraq. The next day they claim to have fired three more missiles and warn Kuwait that it would consider them allowing U.S. planes to base there an "act of war". On Sept 13 Iraq dropped its threat to shoot at U.S. planes and the U.S. says it is sending 5,000 troops to Kuwait.
Sept 14 - Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk pardons dissident Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary for his role in the notorious "killing fields" era of the late 1970s.
Sept 15 - Italy's Northern League Umberto Bossi proclaims the north of the country the "Federal Republic of Padania".
Sept 16 - Romania and Hungary sign a key treaty to end centuries-old disputes.
Sept 16 - Australia and France agree to put aside their differences over French nuclear testing in the South Pacific.
Sept 18 - Over 20 North Korean infiltrators land from a submarine in the South. Most are shot or captured.
Sept 18 - China and its supporters block an attempt to get the General Assembly to consider U.N. membership for Taiwan.
Sept 18 - Results from the Sept 14 election show Bosnia's Moslem President Alija Izetbegovic narrowly defeated Bosnian Serb rival Momcilo Krajisnik.
Sept 19 - A British judge says Robert Maxwell's son Kevin will not face a second trial on charges of alleged fraud.
Sept 20 - Estonian President Lennart Meri is re-elected for a five-year term.
Sept 20 - Murtaza Bhutto, estranged brother of Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, is killed in a gunfight with police in Karachi.
Sept 20 - Russian heart surgeon says President Yeltsin suffered a previously unreported heart attack in late June or early July.
Sept 21 - Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao resigns as head of the Congress Party. Sitaram Kesri is elected to succeed him on the 23rd.
Sept 22 - The Socialists are returned to power in general elections in Greece.
Sept 22 - A cancer victim becomes the first to take his own life under Australia's voluntary euthanasia law. The news is not released until the 26th.
Sept 23 - Four gunmen attack a Sunni Moslem mosque in the Pakistani city of Multan, killing at least 21 people.
Sept 24 - The U.S., China, France, Russia and Britain become the first signatories to a landmark world treaty banning nuclear tests. It had been approved by the General Assembly on the 10th.
Sept 25 - The Afghan Taleban militia capture the strategic town of Sarobi.
Sept 25 - Doctors decide that Boris Yeltsin will undergo heart surgery but set no date. They say it will take six to eight weeks to prepare him.

Sept 25-29 - Fifty-five Palestinians and 14 Israeli soldiers are killed in the worst clashes in the West Bank since PLO rule began two years ago. The fighting was triggered by Israel's opening of a new entrance to a tunnel near Islam's third holiest site, in Jerusalem.
Sept 26 - Hong Kong activist David Chan drowned in the East China Sea after Japanese patrol boats thwarted his protest ship's bid to land on a disputed archipelago.
Sept 26 - U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid returns to earth after 188 days in orbit on the Russian space station Mir, longer than any other American and a record for a woman.
Sept 27 - Afghan capital Kabul falls to Taleban militia. It immediately sets up an Islamic state and executes former president Najibullah.
Sept 27 - Burmese police detain 109 activists and block all roads leading to democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's house.
Sept 30 - Switzerland votes for a sweeping historical study of Swiss financial dealings with Nazi Germany and the fate of Jewish wealth deposited before, during and after World War Two.

Notable deaths in September included: Emily Kngwarreye, Aboriginal artist (2); Bill Monroe, bluegrass musician (9); Ruggero Mastroianni, film editor (9); General Ernesto Geisel, former Brazilian military dictator (12); Jane Baxter, actress (13); Tupac Shakur, U.S. rap star from wounds sustained in an ambush (13); McGeorge Bundy, political analyst and foreign policy adviser to President John F. Kennedy (16); Spiro Agnew, former U.S. vice-president (17); Murtaza Bhutto, the estranged brother of Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto (20); Dorothy Lamour U.S. film actress (21); Mohamed Benahmed, former Algerian prime minister known as Abdelghani (22); Pavel Sudoplatov, Russian spy (24); Nicu Ceausescu, son of executed Romanian dictator Nicolae (26); Mohammed Najibullah, former president of Afghanistan (27).
